source: Sourcery with Molly O'Shea — Nvidia CEO succession, AI selloff, enterprise AI demand, Starship, orbital compute
summary: Grok/xAI's first-party AI revenue is approaching ~$10B and growing very rapidly, significantly underappreciated
summary_extended: Baker argues that xAI's first-party AI product (Grok/Grokbot) is approaching approximately $10 billion in annual revenue, a figure he derives from third-party data rather than direct knowledge. He characterizes this revenue as very high-margin and growing 'really really really fast,' suggesting the business is scaling at a pace that the market has not yet appreciated. Baker personally uses Grokbot more than X (Twitter) itself, citing it as the most valuable AI tool in his own workflow — a qualitative signal of strong product-market fit. The investment implication is that xAI represents a significantly underappreciated AI revenue story, but because xAI is privately held and not US-listed, there is no directly actionable public equity. The closest public proxy would be X Holdings or any future SpaceX/xAI listing, neither of which is currently traded on US exchanges.
detail: Baker estimates based on third-party data that xAI's (SpaceX's) first-party AI business (Grokbot) is approaching $10B in revenue — high-margin and growing 'really really really fast.' confidence_evidence: Baker qualifies with 'I don't know it but if I were to have an estimate based on third party data' — moderate confidence, not direct knowledge. But he frames it as a significant underappreciated data point.
